name: Boiler Degradation Plausibility
anti_triggers: recent combustion evidence shows strong performance
boiler is non-material to the visible cost boundary
physical_basis: Boilers can lose performance through excess air, fouling, cycling, poor heat transfer and weak maintenance execution.
operational_basis: Weak tuning or sequencing can inflate fuel use while being mistaken for unavoidable thermal duty.
financial_mechanism: Fuel cost and maintenance burden can be misframed if boiler degradation is assumed or ignored without evidence.
typical_false_assumption: Fuel intensity automatically proves generic thermal inefficiency or just process load.
hypothesis: Boiler degradation or weak combustion control may be materially affecting thermal economics and should be falsified locally.
rival_hypotheses: thermal duty is structurally explained by load
another subsystem dominates the visible cost story
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: combustion or maintenance evidence shows degradation risk
boiler duty is materially relevant to economics
falsification_conditions: combustion tuning is tight and current
boiler performance is evidenced as adequate
thermal duty is fully explained by process load
allowed_claim_language: Boiler degradation is a plausible thermal-loss hypothesis requiring combustion and maintenance validation.
prohibited_claim_language: This site has an inefficient boiler.
financial_exposure_if_true: maintenance and sequencing action may outrank capital replacement
financial_exposure_if_false: attention should shift to other thermal rivals
stop_conditions: boiler combustion and maintenance evidence are bounded enough to rank materiality
escalation_conditions: field combustion check required only if paper evidence remains insufficient
example_outputs: Before replacing the boiler, determine whether weak tuning or cycling is the real economic driver.
tests: thermal-process and building bundles should admit this when boiler evidence is unresolved
pattern must stay bounded at L2
